Now I've got to build my current, so I can go ahead and test it out for myself. When I go to GDScript to type in, at least the new annotation is present.

Here is an example project: [resource-list.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19230207/resource-list.zip)

Here is the first problem I've encountered:
![godot_reslist](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/986d150a-0ad1-4b06-8d6c-49c26a7e685d)
There is supposed to be an error when the var used is not a Resource or its sub-class.

I've also encountered two pending issues to be resolved afterwards:
~1. There should be only one argument for the annotation, but it hints more to be accepted.~ **Resolved**
    - That's because I've based it on `@export_file(...)`, which accepts multiple arguments. I need to find an annotation that accepts just one argument; `@export_placeholder(...)` should do.
2. Godot crashes when I clicked on the node with the new annotation.

There is one condition that checks for a specific kind, that is used only in `@export`, so I removed it.

As the result, using the new annotation to export a non-Resource gives an error, as it should:
![godot_reslist2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20e9f8c0-cd74-4de4-bd8d-1054bc7e7b59)

That said, when I set it the correct class, it crashes. This is regardless of whether the directory path exists.

[UPDATE] I set the condition such that the directory path has to be absolute. It now give the directory path error as it should:
![godot_reslist3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15b1e9fc-e31b-4934-bcd1-f60ddf7308a0)

So far, godot doesn't crash when I select the node with `@export_from_dir(...)`-exported resource property. However, it does crash when I clicked on the resource property and its drop-down menu. It also crashes when the annotation is `@export()`.

I have tried the following, but none could resolve:
* Making sure `directory_path` in `editor_resource_picker.cpp` is not null (kept anyway to prevent null)
* Include `core/io/dir_acess.h` in `editor_resource_picker.cpp`
----

In the end, I've resolved the crash by checking in `editor\editor_resource_picker.cpp > add_menu_files()` (line 319) whether `edited_resource.is_valid()`, before setting `res_path`.

Here is my next issue: 
![godot_reslist4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24007a5f-2a9f-40c4-9efc-c4775a2a9f19)

Looks like `directory_path` is always set to "res://" regardless of argument.

[UPDATE] The same drop-down appears on `@export()`, too.

[UPDATE] Found the error in the code. In `modules\gdscript\gdscript_parser.cpp` line 4537, `variable->export_info.hint` should be set of `PROPERTY_HINT_RES_FROM_DIR` when it was `PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE`. Resolved by fixing it.

Before rebasing, I want a way to filter the files to show only resources or its sub-classes. As shown on the image above, all files are listed even though some are not appropriate values.

**How do Load and Quick Load filter files?**

In **Load**, `editor/gui/editor_file_dialog.cpp` sets filter first (in `add_filter(...)` on line 1361, filters are added onto `Vector<String> filters` in .h's line 154), then `EditorFileDialog::popup_file_dialog()` in line 200 is called.

`EditorFileDialog::_native_dialog_cb(...)` in line 108 seems to just set files and filters for local variables.

In **Quick Load**, `editor/gui/editor_quick_open_dialog.cpp`, `EditorQuickOpenDialog::popup_dialog(...)` (line 146), arguement `p_base_types` set `Vector<StringName> base_types` in .h's line 113.

`QuickOpenResultContainer::_find_filepaths_in_folder(...)` in line 386 filters files to only include specific classes.

I forgot I should fix `export()` listing file in root project first. Could it be because empty string is treated as root project folder when called by `dir_access->dir_exists_absolute(directory_path)`?

[ADDED] Apparently so, as checking `directory_path` to be empty first resolves the issue.

When I don't put in an argument for `@export_from_dir(...)`, the engine crashes when the property inspector updates the property with that export. By right, it should use "res://" as default.

Typing "res://" for an argument does not crash, though.

Maybe I should take a look at how other export annotations handle default arguments.

[ADDED] Resolved by taking into account whether `args` in `editor > editor_properties.cpp > get_editor_for_property(...)`, line 3820, has element index 1 after split from `p_hint_text`.

Encountered one error output when I set a resource in the editor property:
![godot_reslist6](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe7bde79-bb7a-40de-9f34-b54e838de256)
The error is also printed on console:
```
ERROR: Condition "inheritors_array.is_empty()" is true.
   at: EditorResourcePicker::_edit_menu_cbk (editor\editor_resource_picker.cpp:500)
```
----
I think it happens because clicking on the file from the list calls both `_on_file_pressed()` and `_edit_menu_cbk(...)`. Perhaps creating a new function for file selection from list is a mistake.

[ADDED] I created a new function as it requires the index of the file position from list in order to set the resource. This cannot be done on `_edit_menu_cbk(...)`.

An update to the example project: 
[resource-list.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19535045/resource-list.zip)

This one includes `@export_from_dir(..)` with argument input. It also demonstrates filtering out files.
